correctness.rationale: For each nontrivial vertex cut S with a=|S∩A|, b=|S∩B|, D=a(q-b)+b(p-a), the zonotope support in normal v_S=1_S-s/n*1 is D/2. Coarea/decomposition into cut normals establishes that all these inequalities characterize the whole zonotope, hence c+rB lies within iff |sum_{i in S}c_i|+r sqrt(s(n-s)/n)<=D/2 for every S. The centered optimum radius is min cut normalized support, already known in prior cut theorem. K_{p,q} Laplacian has spectral gap p, yielding D>=p s(n-s)/n. For n>=6 and 2<=s<=n-2, strict 2(n-2)>n^2/(n-1) excludes nonsingletons from radius equality; n=5 (2,3) and n=4 (2,2) are directly exhausted. Active opposite supporting inequalities force B coordinates zero for p<q (rank q); for p=q>=3 every coordinate zero; for (2,2) mixed equalities leave t(1,1,-1,-1). Other cuts are strict at origin, so for p<q full dimension p-1 survives, with exact beta_a=min_b slack inequalities. For p=2, maximizing (b+1)(q+1-b) gives T_q=q/2-sqrt(floor((q+2)^2/4)/(q+1)); binomial endpoint counts follow from its maximizing integers. K_{2,2} singleton bounds yield |t|<=1-sqrt(3)/2 and count eight endpoint oriented facets. Independently enumerated all cut ratios in 20 (p,q) cases with n<=11 using exact integer D^2(n-1)-p^2 s(n-s), confirming active singleton/mixed patterns and radial dimensions. General proof is spectral and uses strict inequalities, not extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge distinct full Chebyshev-center locus classification. The prior general weighted-graph cut theorem gives the inradius and ONE symmetry center, explicitly not all centers. The complete-bipartite Löwner result computes an enclosing ellipsoid and contact *vertices*, not inscribed Euclidean ball centers or contact facets. Deformation/shuffle studies concern combinatorics, not the exact incenter locus. No statement/implication among read sources determines the p-1/0/1 center-dimension phase or p=2 endpoint facets.
residual_risks: Metric classifications of Chebyshev-center polytopes under other terminology may include this family; prior general cut-radius theorem is explicitly acknowledged.
The endpoint facet count is for exact unit-edge Euclidean realization, not arbitrary graph weights.

The p<q vs balanced dimension transition and exceptional K2,2 interval, plus explicit exact center inequalities and parity-sensitive endpoint contact counts, expose a structural change in a canonical geometric optimization problem.
